kept.title: First seven ON-vs-OFF bench versions are INVALIDATED (oracle contamination)
kept.summary: v1-v7 shipped their acceptance tests inside the agent's worktree, so the cold arm reverse-engineered answers from the committed test (caught by the rigging guard on v8). They are gitignored and excluded from the release — make NO claims on them. The shipping benchmark is held-out grading (bench/heldout/): solve from a prose spec, an external suite the agent never sees grades the frozen artifact, and a cold-arm-must-fail guard gates any win claim.

kept.title: Memory helps an agent IFF the fact is empirical, external-to-artifact, and project-local
kept.summary: The only causally-proven win condition: retrieved memory lets the agent solve cases it otherwise can't only when the needed knowledge is (1) empirical, (2) external to the artifact, (3) project-local. Blind-graded held-out: cold scored 0/10 and 0/8 with ZERO variance, warm scored 8.8/10 and 8/8 while writing MORE code (3.8x/1.7x) — so it's retrieve-and-apply, not shortcutting. The winnable slice of note-dependent tasks is ~23% (12/52).

kept.title: ON-vs-OFF cost: real work is parity; the whole delta is cache_read of loaded context
kept.summary: Measured with output tokens (NOT a net metric — the net-metric trap inflates the delta), actual work is parity with/without the graph. The entire cost difference is cache_read of injected context; a compact payload restores parity (cost-weighted gross v2 fat 1.63x -> v3 lean 1.03x). Memory does not help on self-solvable tasks — eight consecutive nulls, with forced context producing up to a ~2x over-deliberation tax that grows monotonically with the amount injected.

kept.title: ORCH_WORKSPACE pins a process's workspace independent of cwd (workspace-gremlin fix)
kept.summary: mcp-graph.js once POSTed process.cwd() as the daemon workspace on startup, so ANY process loading the orchestrator MCP (e.g. a headless agent in a git worktree) hijacked the global state.workspace pointer — repointing the live graph and blinding agents to the real workspace. WS now resolves ORCH_WORKSPACE -> data-dir workspace file -> cwd, and is carried into every MUTATING (POST) tool call so writes land in the calling session's workspace even when another session flipped the global pointer.
kept.evidence: mcp-graph.js:15-19,76; daemon.js:396 (per-request workspace targeting); commit a7166b0

kept.title: One decideAll heartbeat multiplexes N loops keyed by UUID (loops.json registry)
kept.summary: The daemon replaced the singleton `loop` + loop.json with `const loops = new Map()` keyed by UUID, persisted to loops.json (legacy loop.json is migrated into one entry on first boot for upgrade survival). decideOne(L,ctx) decides per-loop; a single batched decideAll() heartbeat advances them all; sweepStaleLoops() is a central liveness sweep (dead session / budget / iterations / no-progress) run in the same pass plus a 60s timer.

kept.title: Autonomous loop HOLDS all code work — never merges to main, queues 'MERGE PENDING'
kept.summary: Every code-producing task the heartbeat loop spawns works in an isolated orch/attempt/<slug> worktree, commits there, and completes as `complete_task(key, 'MERGE PENDING — <branch>: ...')`. The loop never edits the live checkout and never merges; merging to main is a HUMAN decision on review. The self-learn-judge under hold-merge picks a winner but does NOT merge or remove worktrees. (Note: a judge blocked by attempts only becomes ready once EVERY attempt is `done`.)

kept.title: self-register-on-claim: a registered worktree is proof-of-delegation for hook-less workers
kept.summary: The SubagentStart hook never fires for run_in_background Agent-tool spawns, so those workers never carry agent_tool_spawn:true and start_task used to refuse every one ('dispatcher sessions cannot claim') — deadlocking dispatch. Fix: a claim bearing an agent_id AND a registered worktree (only branch_task creates one; the dispatcher never calls it) now self-registers the worker. Claims with no worktree still 409 — the worktree stays the security boundary keeping dispatchers from claiming.

kept.title: orch bash write-gate EXEMPTS git VCS ops (but not working-tree-overwriting subcommands)
kept.summary: git commit/merge/add/push/pull/fetch/branch/tag/worktree/rebase/cherry-pick/log/status/diff/show/rev-parse/describe/remote are exempt from the bash write-gate — they operate on already-claimed work and were tripping the write-pattern detector via '>' chars in commit messages and git-apply heredocs (->, =>, >=). Still GATED (source-overwriting): checkout, restore, reset, clean, rm, stash.

kept.title: /search is bitemporal: asOf (valid-time) + knownAsOf (transaction-time) compose
kept.summary: GET /search supports two independent time axes: asOf returns the note CURRENT at that instant (valid-time), knownAsOf drops hits whose created_at is after T (transaction-time, so a backdated insert can't rewrite earlier-knowledge queries); together they form the canonical bitemporal query. Iterative retrieval uses round (1-based, <3) + exclude_keys, returning continue=true iff a NEW note scored >=0.5. Gotcha: the FIRST gated call may take 10-90s while MiniLM lazy-loads; embed() degrading to null => all-zero scores => abstain (never a hard failure).

kept.title: Git ops target resolveRepo(): explicit repo_path > task's overlay repo > daemon workspace
kept.summary: resolveRepo(key, explicit) decouples the loop's git target from the daemon's own workspace, so branch/merge/measure can run on a client repo distinct from the workspace. Precedence is request-body repo_path > the task's overlay `repos[key]` field (set via configure_task repo_path) > state.workspace (back-compat default).

kept.title: Ingest pipeline mines git/docs/structure — reverts & fixes are the delta over current code
kept.summary: Cold-start is dissolved by scripts/ingest-{git,docs,structure}.js, which mine an existing codebase into the task/note/context graph: commit history (precise gotchas/decisions — especially reverts/fixes, which encode knowledge NOT visible by reading current code), distilled docs/ADRs into decision/constraint notes, and the static module-dependency graph. Mined JSON + reviewed candidates land under bench/ingest/.

kept.title: /agent/done cascades to release the held in_progress claim; releaseClaim reverts native status
kept.summary: A claim is a status OVERRIDE, not a terminal state. /agent/done releases the agent's held in_progress task (fixing phantom in_progress), and the staleness sweep auto-releases abandoned claims (kill/crash/idle/cross-session). releaseClaim also reverts the NATIVE status (which start_task wrote to in_progress via write-through) back to pending — otherwise the task would still derive in_progress from its stub file.

kept.title: get_learnings returns a digested rejected[] ledger so planners skip losing approaches
kept.summary: digestRejected(verdicts, failures, labelFor) turns nested verdicts into a flat rejected[] ledger — verdict losers as {approach, reason, beatenBy, source:'verdict'} and genuine dead-end failures as {approach, reason, source:'failure'} — explicitly EXCLUDING superseded/duplicate/consolidated entries. The planner scans it in one pass to dedup against approaches already tried, instead of hand-parsing nested verdicts.

kept.title: Only the PRIMARY checkout compacts .graph; worktree daemons must skip it
kept.summary: Attempt-branch worktree daemons share tracked .graph history with main, so compacting it independently GUARANTEES merge conflicts when the attempt lands. Compaction (folding per-node jsonl into the checkpoint, +24h interval) is gated on isPrimaryCheckout() — the mechanical test is whether .git is a directory (primary) vs a file/gitdir pointer (worktree); a worktree daemon logs 'skipped — not the primary checkout'.

kept.title: Embeddings are a local detached MiniLM sidecar (Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim), no hosted API
kept.summary: lib/embed.js delegates to lib/embed-server.js running Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 → 384 floats, no hosted API and no vector DB. The sidecar is spawned detached+unref'd on the first embed() call so it OUTLIVES daemon restarts — the 10-90s model load (~90MB download, first run only) happens at most once per machine session, not per daemon restart. embed() returns null (→ all-zero scores → abstain) while loading.

kept.title: orch-gate denies a write (exit 2) unless HEAD is on the task's registered orch/attempt/* branch
kept.summary: hooks/orch-gate.sh reads the task's registered git.branch; if the task has a registered worktree but the writing actor's HEAD is not on an orch/attempt/* branch, it hard-blocks with exit 2 ('writes must happen inside the worktree branch'). This is the enforcement behind the branch_task-before-writing contract — a subagent must write inside the worktree path, never on the session root (which sits on main).

kept.title: suggest_links flags duplicate only at score >= 0.6 against an OPEN non-note task
kept.summary: SUGGEST_DUP_THRESHOLD = 0.6 is the shipped cutoff: a candidate is marked duplicate:true only when label/summary overlap >= 0.6 AND the matched task is OPEN AND not a note (catching re-plan duplicates). suggest_kind is 'context' for notes/done tasks, 'blocking' otherwise.
